@@ -44,7 +44,8 @@ a <- 55
 | **Predicate/bang names** | an identifier may carry a single trailing `?` or `!` — `empty?`, `gate!` | The family convention (Elixir/Ruby/Crystal): `?` reads "predicate", `!` "stricter/effecting variant". `?` is otherwise unused in the grammar (zero ambiguity); a trailing `!` is part of the name only when it does not begin the `!=` operator (`a!=b` ≡ `a != b`). The codepoint survives to each target's symbol table (BEAM `empty?/1`). |
 | **Keyword field labels** | a reserved keyword may label a field — `Field(type: t)`, `%{case: c}` | In label position (`word :`) the keyword cannot be a declaration, so it is unambiguously a field name. Matches Elixir (`%{type: 1}`) and avoids forcing renames of common Elixir/IR field names (`type`, `def`) on the way into Rian. Applies to named construction, map literals, and the symmetric patterns. |
 | **As-patterns** | `name @ pat` binds the whole value while matching `pat` (Core `PAs`) | The capture every AST walk needs (`node @ {:bin, op, l, r}`). `@` is the operator (spaced — `@name` without a space stays the annotation lane); the binder is a plain variable. Lowers to Erlang `Name = Pat`, Elixir `pat = name`, Rust `name @ pat`. |
-| **Map update** | `%{base \| k: v, …}` replaces the named keys on an existing map (Core `EMapUpdate`) | Elixir's spelling, reusing the `%{…}` lexeme and the existing `\|` token. Disambiguated from a literal by the first form after `%{` (a `key:` is a literal; anything else is an update base, parsed up to `\|`). Every updated key must already be present — BEAM `:map_field_exact` (`:=`), JS object spread (`{...base, k: v}`); BEAM-only on the Rust/JVM PoC, like map literals. |
+| **Map update** | `%{base \| k: v, …}` replaces the named keys on an existing map (Core `EMapUpdate`) | Elixir's spelling, reusing the `%{…}` lexeme and the existing `\|` token. Disambiguated from a literal by the first form after `%{`: a `key:` is a literal; anything else parses one expression, then `\|` ⇒ an update base, `=>` ⇒ a non-atom-key literal (below). Every updated key must already be present — BEAM `:map_field_exact` (`:=`), JS object spread (`{...base, k: v}`); BEAM-only on the Rust/JVM PoC, like map literals. |
+| **Non-atom map keys** | `%{keyExpr => v, …}` (and in patterns / updates) keys a map by an arbitrary expression, not just an atom label (Core pair `{{:key, expr}, value}`) | Elixir's `=>` spelling, reusing the `%{…}` lexeme and a new `=>` token. The `k: v` shorthand stays the common atom-key case; `=>` covers string/module/tuple/computed keys (`%{"a" => 1}`, `%{Mod => …}`). A map pattern `%{k => p}` looks the value up at the **key value** (the key is an expression, `p` the bound sub-pattern). **BEAM-only**: the BEAM lowers it natively (`:map_field_assoc`/`:map_field_exact` with the key expression) and `Rian.Lower`'s Elixir text emits `k => v`, but a JS object coerces keys to strings (a module/tuple key would collide), so `Rian.JS` raises and `Rian.Reach` pins a computed-key map off `:rs`/`:js`/`:jvm` (atom-key maps keep their `:ex`+`:js` reach). String-key JS support is a deliberate follow-on. |
 
 ### Guards keep `when` — resolved by the Elixir `case` form
